newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil tanker prepares for trans-shipment.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil tanker prepares for trans-shipment.

text.p: Venezuela's National Contingency Plan (NCP) said Thursday the striken Nissos Amorgos oil tanker would be moved closer to shore to undertake trans-shipment of the remaining crude oil on the vessel.

The ship ran aground in the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel on Friday 28 February spilling about 25,000 barrels of heavy crude and has been sitting on anchor 14 miles off the northern Venezuela coast since Saturday March 1.

The NCP is hoping to move the ship to a new position nine miles offshore to allow divers to inspect initial repairs made to stem the oil spill. After the inspection, the NCP hopes to move the tanker within three miles of the coast to trans-ship the crude into another tanker in calmer weather conditions.
A strong wind was blowing when the tanker ran aground carrying 476,000 barrels of crude, and these conditions hampered early attempts to stem the oil spill.
The NCP said 2,876 cubic metres of contaminated material had been collected from 44 kilometres of coastline near the spill and 13 kilometres of coast remained to be cleaned.
